explicit_summary_lines: „Kit übernehmen“ raises the Cockpit’s own build revision once its local check passed, so an adoption that leaves an Unreleased line (Kit 1.4.0, K4) needs no follow-up PR; on chore/kit-<version> the stale-app guard shows that revision as a note instead of locking „Abschließen“ (plan C2).

The release rule reads the work order's calls, not its text: an execute flag in a docstring or a pull-request body no longer turns a dry run of release-publish or release run into a live run (no rejection, no approval question), a live call is judged by its own flags or by an execute flag standing free in the code, and every rejection names the call and its line (AGP_RELEASE_RULE_CALLS_V1, plan C1); build `release-0.4.1-r2`.

„Abschließen“ knows committed, unpublished work: on a clean work branch with own commits the Lage says whether they are on GitHub, the finish prompt states that the Kit publishes existing commits without a path selection (Kit 1.4.0, K1) and names no Kit command, and the finish guard, which still forbids a new commit there, also rejects a finish call that selects paths and names the call and its line (AGP_FINISH_PUBLISH_EXISTING_V1, plan C3); build `release-0.4.1-r3`.

„Release“ runs the Kit's read check before it asks: the repository's Kit answers `release ready` for the version (step A2 of its release run), and only its PASS leads to the question; any other answer shows the Kit's stopped steps, check id and resolving command with its consent flag, or its reason, and nothing starts. The Cockpit judges nothing itself; a resumed release skips the check (AGP_RELEASE_READ_CHECK_V1, plan C4); build `release-0.4.1-r4`.

The Kit findings window shows the installed Kit's catalog entries that the Cockpit's register does not list (KIT-GF-090, 096–098 and 100–120 at Kit 1.4.0) as a group of their own below the register: the Kit answers `greenfield status --json` beside the UI thread, the Cockpit reads only id, title, Kit state, fixed in and the report name, judges nothing and never writes them into its register; without a Kit or an answer the window names the reason (AGP_KIT_CATALOG_GROUP_V1, plan C5); build `release-0.4.1-r5`.

The Claude chat handoff works with clones instead of folder access: `scripts/claude_handoff.py write` no longer takes `--host-root`, its start sentence asks for anonymous full clones of the Cockpit and the Kit and for `check <handoff file>` with the handoff from an attachment or project file, `check` refuses a shallow clone and, without a file in a clone, asks for the attachment; no app or extension code changed, build stays `release-0.4.1-r5` (AGP_CLAUDE_HANDOFF_CLONES_V1, plan C6).

An open question of „Abschließen“ closes when the work was published outside the task: once the Lage is BEREIT, the Kit's post-merge check passes and the commit the task started on is in origin/main (the criterion of the late-completion check), the question box closes, the light follows the Lage and the status line says that the question is overtaken and nothing was executed; no decision is recorded and the mission is not touched. The start commit is stored per task in the runtime folder, so this also holds for a question adopted after a restart, and a question rejected before a restart is no longer shown again; other tasks keep asking (AGP_DECISION_OVERTAKEN_V1, plan C7); build `release-0.4.1-r6`.

A background worker of the UI no longer holds its window: the Lage, „Branch wechseln“, the Systemcheck and the Kit findings sync give their worker threads plain values only (path, flag, binary). A worker that outlived its window kept it alive, and the window was later freed on a foreign thread: with Python 3.12 (CI) Tcl aborts the process, with Python 3.14 (the owner's Mac) the Tcl interpreter is leaked with a warning. The SIGTRAP of long Tk test runs on the Mac is not explained by this (corrected after order 2309). A test guards every worker of a Tk module, and a probe process shows the abort or the leak on the previous code (AGP_TK_WORKER_PLAIN_VALUES_V1); build `release-0.4.1-r7`.

Long Tk test runs on the Mac no longer abort with SIGTRAP: Tk 9 on macOS schedules a one-time idle task for the first root window of a process, so a first test window destroyed before an idle pass left the task pointing at a freed window, and the next test's `update()` or `update_idletasks()` crashed in `showRootWindow` (Mac crash reports of 2026-11-15; freeing the first Tk object does not prevent it). The test session now runs that task on a throwaway root before any test window exists; a macOS test and a probe process cover it (AGP_TK_FIRST_ROOT_IDLE_V1). Tests only.
